decision: Lead with the Quadrantids and make the peak-time mismatch the story; skip the New Moon, Venus and the planetary scan
rationale: The Quadrantids peak at 19:37 CET on 3 Jan, when the radiant is only ~10 deg up in the north, so the honest angle is 'the peak happens before the radiant is high, the real window is before dawn'. That is more useful than a generic 'meteor shower tonight'. A 12% Moon 5 deg up barely interferes. New Moon on 7 Jan is not a viewing event, and the planetary scan repeats every week.
alternatives: Present the peak as the viewing time (rejected: radiant only ~10 deg up, misleading)
Lead with Venus at 17 deg (rejected: weak altitude)
Ignore the shower in a quiet week (rejected: it is the strongest event of the window)

decision: Hook rewritten to 'The year's first big meteor shower peaks this weekend.' followed by the before-dawn-Monday advice.
rationale: The old first sentence was 15 words and opened on a negative (radiant barely above the horizon); the first line must land the promise in ~3 s.
